posts.title: W.D. Tex., Pro Se Staff Attorney announcement (July 2026): Pro Se Law Clerk, multiple locations including Waco and Austin
posts.body:
The U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas is hiring Pro Se Law Clerks (the court's pro se staff attorneys), assigned to the district judges' chambers.
Locations: Austin, Del Rio, El Paso, Midland, San Antonio and Waco; multiple positions.
Salary: $74,678 to $168,110 (JSP 11 to 14), depending on qualifications.
Open until filled; immediate start. Positions are funded through at least December 31, 2028.
Duties: legal research, bench memoranda and draft orders on pro se matters, docket management, including prisoner petitions and civil rights complaints.
Qualifications: graduation from an accredited law school. Hiring is subject to a fingerprint background check and credit check.
How to apply: through OSCAR (oscar.uscourts.gov): Positions > All Positions, search "Alia Moses". Read the full announcement (PDF, updated July 20, 2026) before applying; it controls over this summary.
Pinned by Legal Luminary as thread -1 until removed. Legal Luminary is not affiliated with the court and does not accept applications.
posts.source_label: Posted by Scott Weeden (from the court's announcement)

posts.title: Opportunity discovered: an advertisement-free, verified information site for the Office of the Mayor of Killeen
posts.body:
Opportunity discovered: accurate, authoritative information for Killeen residents without the bias of financial or undue political influence. The City's own City Council web page still lists an outgoing mayor months after the May 2, 2026 election; mayors elsewhere use simple mayor-named domains such as mayorbrown.com.
Cloud Fronts Group proposes an informational site at mayor[surname].com for whoever is the elected Mayor: plain-language explanations of notices and new laws, mirroring (never replacing) killeentexas.gov, automatic inclusion of KISD Board of Trustees announcements from its official channels, and every elected official included regardless of politics or social media platform.
Advertising is 100% restricted: no ads, sponsored content or promotional offers of any kind.
No notice is posted without three sign-offs: a witness, the Council Member for the district concerned, and the Mayor. Law enforcement provides updates on public-safety notices.
The full proposal is a printable agreement with signature lines for the Mayor, a majority of the City Council, the City Manager, the KISD Board, the law enforcement agency, Cloud Fronts Group and a witness; no party is bound until it signs.
Disclosure: posted by the operator of Legal Luminary, a partner in Cloud Fronts Group. Not endorsed or accepted by the Mayor or the City.
posts.source_label: Posted by Scott Weeden (partner, Cloud Fronts Group)

posts.title: Seeking counsel on contingency (33%): Weeden v. United States et al., W.D. Tex. (Waco) — quiet title and wrongful foreclosure
posts.body:
Plaintiff Scott Weeden, individually and as trustee of the Weeden Family Trust, is preparing a federal complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas, Waco Division, and seeks counsel admitted in that district.
Defendants: the United States (HUD), Onity Mortgage f/k/a PHH Mortgage Corporation, Servis One, Inc. d/b/a BSI Financial Services, and Quality Loan Service Corporation.
Claims in the draft: quiet title against the United States (28 U.S.C. 2409a) and as to a HUD partial-claim lien the plaintiff says he never signed (28 U.S.C. 2410); wrongful foreclosure under the Oregon Trust Deed Act (no channel to cure, refused pre-sale tender, lis pendens recorded before the 2023 trustee's sale); breach of contract and good faith; RESPA notice-of-error (12 U.S.C. 2605); declaratory and injunctive relief. The property is a home in Portland, Oregon.
Relief sought: return of title, or just compensation; lost equity of $66,854.73, $25,000 in improvements and $36,500 restitution; in the alternative not less than $250,000.
Status: draft complaint for attorney review, motion to proceed in forma pauperis and motion for appointment of counsel prepared; exhibits A-F (servicing records, notice of sale, unsigned partial-claim deed of trust, notice of error, payment history, recorded deed) and a recorded servicer call transcript are available to counsel on request.
Offer: Plaintiff offers a contingency fee of 33% of any recovery, on a written agreement signed by Plaintiff and counsel. Interested attorneys: email meseeks@legalluminary.com with the subject line of this post.
posts.source_label: Posted by the plaintiff, Scott Weeden

posts.title: HUD notice of default and foreclosure sale, Temple property: sale November 3, 2026
posts.body:
Issuer: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, through its designated foreclosure commissioner (Single Family Mortgage Foreclosure Act of 1994, 12 U.S.C. 3751 et seq.). TS No. LO-54089-TX.
Nonjudicial foreclosure of a HUD-held deed of trust on residential property in Temple, Texas (Bell County).
Sale: Tuesday, November 3, 2026, between 10:00 AM and 1:00 PM, at public auction at the Bell County Clerk's alcove, Bell County Justice Complex, 1201 Huey Drive, Belton, Texas (or the area designated by the Commissioners Court).
Reinstatement: the notice states the amount required to reinstate before the sale, as of November 2, 2026. Bidders other than HUD must bring a 10% deposit by certified or cashier's check.
Published in the Killeen Daily Herald on October 1, 8 and 15, 2026.
Borrower names and the property address are in the published notice linked below; they are not repeated here.

posts.title: Representation opportunity: defendants in two Bell County title and lien suits (25DCV352411, 26DCV360297)
posts.body:
Defendants served by publication in two Bell County district court suits brought by mortgage lenders may need counsel before their answer deadlines: Cause No. 25DCV352411 (146th District Court, answer due by our count October 26, 2026) and Cause No. 26DCV360297 (169th District Court, answer due by our count November 16, 2026). Both concern title to residential property in Temple and Killeen; one includes the unknown heirs of a deceased borrower.
Legal Luminary does not represent these defendants and does not make offers or agree to fee terms on their behalf. Party information is in the public notices and the court files. Attorneys interested in defense, heirship, or title work in Bell County can review the files with the Bell County District Clerk and contact the parties directly, consistent with the Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct.
A printable contingency fee agreement template is linked below. A defendant may choose to use it with an attorney willing to take the matter on contingency; it binds no one unless both the defendant and the attorney complete and sign it.
If you are a defendant in one of these cases, consider contacting a lawyer before the deadline. Lone Star Legal Aid and TexasLawHelp.org can help you find free or low-cost help.
posts.source_label: Witnessed by Scott Weeden (Killeen Daily Herald legal notices)
